note: Stage 2d (22 Nov 2026, docs/design/ANIMAL_ROUTINES_TRAILS_TRAPPING.md, TR-13): signs along the trails, worked out on each client from the routes it already has (same spots for every player, no server cost). Rabbits leave pellet latrines by the warren and at the grazing end of a run and dig scrapes where runs of different warrens meet; deer leave prints where a trail crosses wet ground and droppings by the bed (Ziege et al. 2016, BMC Ecology, rabbit latrines; onX and Idaho Fish and Game on deer sign). A player sees them from Tracking skill see_level (latrines and droppings) and fine_level (scrapes and prints; both 0 since Dave's 23 Nov 2026 ruling that signs are simply there for everyone, see everyone_note; they were 5 and 25), within draw_m (min at see_level, max at 100). Nothing is made before the player has ground (the first-join window). Provisional.
spot_note: Spotting (Dave 23 Nov 2026: 'spotting animal markings should highlight the markings, make a slight sound and give xp for finding them'): a shown sign the player first comes within spot_m of glows for glow_s (a soft pale patch, glow_color, up to glow_alpha), the slight sound sign_spot plays there (batch3_slots.json) and the server trains Tracking once per sign (traps.json tracking sign_*); one sign every spot_gap_s, so each of a cluster is trained (the practice cooldown is 2 s).
everyone_note: Dave 23 Nov 2026: 'signs should just be there and if you have a higher tracking skill maybe they get highlighted or glow a little'. Every kind of sign shows to everyone from the first level (see_level and fine_level 0); Tracking only reaches farther (draw_m, 15 m untrained to 30 m at 100) and, from halo_from, lays a faint steady pale patch under each shown sign (halo_alpha from halo_from to 100, lit like the ground, so dark at night: the eye catching it, not a marker). The spot glow, sound and XP stay as they were. Provisional.
latrine_note: Lane A 23 Nov 2026 (Job S): 8 to 15 pellets of 1.6 cm at ground level under leaf litter and grass did not show at all. A latrine is now 30 to 50 pellets of about 2 cm on a dark scratched-earth patch about 0.65 m across (real rabbit latrines hold dozens to hundreds of pellets, often on a scraped patch), lifted 2 cm over the litter; deer droppings 15 to 25.
bed_note: Deer beds (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread; Dave: 'extrapolate from them and see what would make for a fun hunting game'): deer lie up by day in small groups, each leaving an oval of pressed grass or leaves about its body's size, the plainest sign that a trail's end is a bedding place (Penn State Extension and onX on deer beds). bed_count beds within bed_off_m of each deer trail's home; grass_view presses the grass in bed_size_m ovals (the worn-earth ground bares the litter there), so no mesh. Provisional.
rub_note: Rubbed trees (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread): stags (and elk, moose) rub the bark off saplings and small trunks along their trails and near beds, a pale strip at knee to chest height that shows from far off (onX 'How to read deer sign'; Texas Parks and Wildlife hunter education). Along each deer trail at most one every rub_every_m, the thinnest loaded trunk up to rub_max_r_m within rub_m of the trail; the strip rub_height_m up its trail side. Provisional.
read_note: Reading a sign (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread): look at a sign within read_m and press E. Anyone reads what it is and who left it (Dave: signs are there for everyone); from read_way_level (the Tracking the Map shows trails at, Dave's 10) which way the trail runs from it and to what; from read_habit_level (Advanced, Dave's skill classes) when the animal uses it, from the routines (rabbits out from about sunset to sunrise, deer feed at dusk and bed by day). Texts after Sal's animal_sign.json hints. Provisional.

latrine.what: A heap of small round pellets on scratched earth. Rabbits mark their run here.
latrine.habit: Rabbits come out along it from about sunset and are back underground after sunrise.

scrape.what: A shallow scrape where two rabbit runs meet.
scrape.habit: Rabbits from two warrens cross here at night: a good place for a snare.

prints.what: Split hoof prints pressed in the soft ground. Deer passed here.
prints.habit: Deer walk this way to feed at dusk and back to their beds at dawn.

droppings.what: A pile of dark pellets. Deer lie up close by.
droppings.habit: Deer bed near here through the day.

bed.what: An oval of pressed-down grass. A deer lay here.
bed.habit: Deer lie here by day and leave at dusk: come quietly, downwind.

rub.what: Bark rubbed off a young tree. A stag marked his trail.
rub.habit: Stags walk this trail between the beds and the feeding ground.
